text:
$400 GTA 6 Collector's Edition Is Missing One Important Item - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
Rockstar has revealed a pricey $400 collector's edition for Grand Theft Auto 6—and it doesn't even include the game. The set does include collectibles such as a pair of Oakley sunglasses, a fanny pack, hat, stickers, a keychain, shot glass, and more. But, for $400 you'd think they toss in a code for GTA 6. In other news, Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still in development at Ubisoft, and has even added a writer from Assassin's Creed Shadows to its team. The game was first announced 18 (!) years ago, and Ubisoft has been drip-feeding updates every few years, with no release date in sight. And finally, Bethesda's Starfield may not be getting a sequel that diehard fans were hoping for, as a former developer admits the game was just not succesful enough.

text:
Garfield - Escape from Monday Review
Garfield - Escape from Monday reviewed by Sarah Thwaites on PC.

"Garfield - Escape from Monday is a mediocre 3D platformer, dragged down by its relentless self-deprecating humor and sluggish platforming. The power-boosting costumes and wonderful, food-flavored set dressings do their best to capture some of the nostalgic joy of Garfield’s past comics and cartoons, but the cat himself is a bitter imitation of those depictions. Mix in some cute but largely pointless collectibles and a camera you occasionally have to fight, and Escape from Monday feels like a step backwards in an era with so many other original and experimental platformers to choose from."

author: IGN YouTube
text:
Halloween: The Game Review
Halloween: The Game reviewed by Vikki Blake on PlayStation 5, also available on PC and Xbox.

"It's difficult to recommend Halloween: The Game to anyone other than a horror fan with a Michael Myers shrine in their home — now that's a scary thought — or those with deep, deep affection for asymmetrical games. It has some good ideas, some of which aren't fully realized, leaving you with a buggy experience that lacks the variety needed to carry asym games, despite the very welcome addition of a single-player campaign. It's not worth remaining in the lobby long after you're dead — even though you lose XP by quitting before the game ends — and if that's not indicative of how Halloween: The Game just hasn't evolved with the genre, we don't know what is."

text:
V/H/S/MIXTAPE - Official Trailer (2026)
Check out the trailer for V/H/S/MIXTAPE, an upcoming horror film featuring new segments from directors Ernest Dickerson, Flying Lotus, Tobias Forge, David Moreau, RZA, and Renee Zhan. The latest installment pushes the boundaries of found footage with four wildly original stories that each put a unique spin on the terrifying relationship between sound and fear. V/HS/MIXTAPE features GWAR and Jim Henson's Creature Shop. 

V/H/S/MIXTAPE cranks the franchise's signature found-footage horror up to eleven with an electrifying new anthology where music and sound become the source of terror. United by a theme that explores the power of music, rhythm, and audio to haunt, possess, transform, and destroy, the film blends cosmic horror, psychological suspense, outrageous splatter, and groundbreaking practical effects into one unforgettable mixtape of nightmares.

V/H/S/MIXTAPE is produced by Josh Goldbloom, Steven Schneider, Roy Lee, Michael Schreiber, and Brad Miska. Ben Ross and Rami Yasin serve as executive producers. It is written by Zoe Cooper, David Moreau, Ernest Dickerson, RZA, and Matt Landsman.

V/H/S/MIXTAPE streams on Shudder beginning October 9, 2026.
